    // # Parameterized easing curves — IProcedural<Number, Number> Eval bodies

    // The Y coordinate of the cubic Bezier with endpoints (0, 0) and (1, 1) and
    // control points (P1.X, P1.Y), (P2.X, P2.Y), evaluated at parameter t.
    Eval(self: CubicBezierEasing, t: Number): Number
        => 0.0.CubicBezier(self.P1.Y, self.P2.Y, 1.0, t);

    // A CSS-style stepped easing: the StepPosition selects where each jump lands
    // within its interval (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Step_function).
    Eval(self: StepEasing, t: Number): Number
        => match (self.Position) {
            JumpStart =>
                (((t * self.Steps.ToNumber).Floor + 1.0) / self.Steps.ToNumber).Min(1.0);
            JumpEnd =>
                t.StaircaseFloor(self.Steps);
            JumpNone =>
                self.Steps <= 1
                    ? t
                    : (t * self.Steps.ToNumber + 0.5).Floor / self.Steps.ToNumber;
            JumpBoth =>
                self.Steps <= 1
                    ? t
                    : ((t * (self.Steps - 1).ToNumber).Floor + 1.0) / self.Steps.ToNumber;
        };
```

    // Order 0 is linear; 1 is cubic smoothstep; 2 is quintic smootherstep; higher
    // orders fall back to linear until a closed form is added.
    Eval(self: SmoothstepEasing, t: Number): Number
        => self.Order == 0 ? t
         : self.Order == 1 ? t.SmoothStep
         : self.Order == 2 ? t.SmootherStep
         : t;
```

    // The classic easing curve at normalized time t.
    Eval(self: ClassicEasing, t: Number): Number
        => match (self) {
            Linear => t;
            Eased(family, phase) => EaseAt(family, phase, t);
        };
}
